name.text: Calculating the area of a rhombus

questiontext.text:
The perimeter of a rhombus is \({@Perimeter@}\text{ m}\). One of its diagonals is \({@One_diagonal@}\text{ m}\).

[[jsxgraph width="500px" height="300px"]] var d1 = {#One_diagonal#}; var d2 = {#other_diagonal#}; var p = {#Perimeter#}; // Half diagonals for drawing var a = d1 / 2; var b = d2 / 2; var ratio = 500 / 300; var spanX = Math.max(d1 * 1.3, d2 * 1.3 * ratio); var spanY = spanX / ratio; var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, { boundingbox: [-spanX/2, spanY/2, spanX/2, -spanY/2], maxboundingbox: [-spanX*1.5, spanY*1.5, spanX*1.5, -spanY*1.5], axis: false, showCopyright: false, keepAspectRatio: true, showNavigation: true }); var p1 = board.create('point', [a, 0], {name: '', visible: false}); var p2 = board.create('point', [0, b], {name: '', visible: false}); var p3 = board.create('point', [-a, 0], {name: '', visible: false}); var p4 = board.create('point', [0, -b], {name: '', visible: false}); var center = board.create('point', [0,0], {name: '', visible: false}); // Rhombus board.create('polygon', [p1, p2, p3, p4], { fillColor: 'none', strokeColor: '#1976d2', strokeWidth: 2 }); // Diagonals board.create('segment', [p3, p1], {dash: 2, strokeColor: '#90caf9'}); board.create('segment', [p4, p2], {dash: 2, strokeColor: '#90caf9'}); // Right angle marker at intersection var rad = Math.min(a, b) * 0.15; board.create('angle', [p1, center, p2], {type: 'square', radius: rad, strokeColor: '#90caf9', name: ''}); // Tightened pixel gaps to keep labels close to the lines var gapY = spanY * 0.015; var gapX = spanX * 0.015; // Dynamic Labels board.create('text', [a/2, -gapY, "d_1 = " + d1 + " m"], {anchorX: 'middle', anchorY: 'top', fontSize: 14}); board.create('text', [-gapX, b/2, "d_2 = ?"], {anchorX: 'right', anchorY: 'middle', fontSize: 14, strokeColor: '#c62828'}); [[/jsxgraph]]

  1. Find the length of the other diagonal (\(d_2\)).

    \(d_2 = \) [[input:ans1]] \(\text{m}\) [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

  2. Find the area of the rhombus.

    \(\text{Area} = \) [[input:ans2]] \(\text{m}^2\) [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

Step 1: Find the length of one side

A rhombus has 4 equal sides. Therefore:

\[ \begin{aligned} \text{Perimeter} &= 4 \times \text{side} \\ {@Perimeter@} &= 4 \times \text{side} \\ \text{side} &= \frac{{@Perimeter@}}{4} \\ \text{side} &= {@c@} \text{ m} \end{aligned} \]

Step 2: Use the diagonal property

The diagonals of a rhombus cut each other into two equal parts and intersect at right angles.

  • One diagonal is \({@One_diagonal@}\text{ m}\), so half of it is \(\frac{{@One_diagonal@}}{2} = {@a@}\text{ m}\).
  • Let the other diagonal be \(d_2\). Half of it is \(\frac{d_2}{2}\).

Using Pythagoras’ Theorem on one of the inner right-angled triangles:

\[ \begin{aligned} \text{side}^2 &= \left( \frac{d_1}{2} \right)^2 + \left( \frac{d_2}{2} \right)^2 \\ {@c@}^2 &= ({@a@})^2 + \left( \frac{d_2}{2} \right)^2 \\ \left( \frac{d_2}{2} \right)^2 &= {@c@}^2 - {@a@}^2 \\ \frac{d_2}{2} &= \sqrt{{@c^2@} - {@a^2@}} \\ \frac{d_2}{2} &= {@b@} \end{aligned} \]

Multiply by 2 to find the full length of the other diagonal:

\[ \begin{aligned} d_2 &= 2 \times {@b@} \\ d_2 &= {@other_diagonal@} \text{ m} \end{aligned} \]

Step 3: Find the area of the rhombus

The formula for the area of a rhombus is \(\text{Area} = \frac{d_1 \times d_2}{2}\).

\[ \begin{aligned} \text{Area} &= \frac{{@One_diagonal@} \times {@other_diagonal@}}{2} \\ \text{Area} &= {@Area_of_Rhombus@} \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned} \]
